chapter: Boyhood in Webster Groves and early roadhouse work
title: Uncle Floyd's blues records
summary: His neighbor Uncle Floyd Thomas played blues records by Mamie Smith, Bessie Smith, Sara Martin and Ma Rainey, and Thomas muses on what makes the blues.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Where the blues came from: Handy, Bolden and early blues

blocks.x: the alleyway or right next door -- you know how it is in the country, you're not across the alleyway, you're right next door-- a man had a lot of influence, I mean, to me. He'd play all the blues records. That was my uncle, my Uncle Floyd. Uncle Floyd Thomas. I've got to mention him because a lot of things I heard that's the first time I heard them, you know.
Oh, this was where you would hear these blues records?

Yeah. Of course, now you know you can hear the blues, the blues is a tune. It's a tune, it's appeal a-feel, it's a lot of things, it's expression. And when it comes in the hands of people who can do it, that's a different interpretation and hasn't that hasn't changed as of today. I don't think so, do you?
Well, (...) have all these records and ...
Well, I mean some people, everybody played the blues but some could put some feeling in them and make them mean something and others, it was nothing.
Well, thank you. That's what I was trying to say. That was exactly what I was trying to say.
Well, he'd have his records and these records would be Mamie Smith, Bessie Fletcher Smith, Sara Martin, Ma Rainey, you know.
Of course, when you hear those, now you're beginning to hear the people that played on those records, too, as well as the singers.

Well, yes, I am. I think what I'm doing, too, yes I am, Stanley. I think what I'm doing, too, there might be -- yes, these are right in those years. You're quite right about too that and the thing that happened too -- you going to mention Helen?

I don't see why we shouldn't, Stanley. You got it on, you got it off, huh? I don't see why we shouldn't. I think it might have happened during that time, Stan, because I'm beginning to get a chance to get acquainted with the cornet.
